concepts.def: Energy goes to PE, not KE

walkthroughs.body_html:
pV = constant when temperature is constant.

Halve V -> double p.
All input energy goes into breaking bonds (PE) not faster motion (KE).

Squeezing a gas does work on it -> internal energy rises -> temperature rises.

Used in bike pumps and engines.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
